1	# Fire Yourselves — Build Plan
2	
3	**Product working name:** Redline
4	**One-liner:** Reads a chart against a federal regulation and cites every place the regulation isn't satisfied — or the place the documentation should have been.
5	**Constraint:** 4 hours build, 3:00 live demo, one shot, judges supply/modify input.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. The single most important decision
10	
11	**Rulebook = 42 CFR §482.61, not ASAM and not TJC CTS.**
12	
13	Your take-home README already establishes why: the ASAM 4th-edition PDF carries an explicit no-AI-input prohibition, and the TJC public portal signals `ai-train=no` plus AI-crawler `Disallow`. Every `requirement_text` in `app/intelligence/compliance/standards.py` is therefore an original paraphrase.
14	
15	For a *demo*, a paraphrased rule is unverifiable. The judge reads a requirement they can't check against a source you can't show.
16	
17	§482.61 is US federal regulation — public domain, no copyright, no robots restriction. Consequences:
18	
19	- **Verbatim requirement text on screen.** The exact regulatory language, next to the chart excerpt.
20	- **A judge can verify on their phone** at ecfr.gov during the demo.
21	- **No IP disclosure section needed**, no paraphrase-quality risk, no awkward question.
22	
23	It also keeps the healthcare-compliance story intact: TJC accreditation is used for *deemed status* against these same CMS Conditions of Participation. Say that once, move on.
24	
25	**Action in hour 1:** pull §482.61 from https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-482/subpart-E/section-482.61 and commit the raw text to `rules/482_61_source.txt`. Verbatim. This is your source of truth and your on-screen citation.
26

29	## 1. What to port from `perspectives-take-home`, and what to cut
30	
31	### Port (this is your head start — do not rebuild)
32	
33	| From repo | Why |
34	|---|---|
35	| `app/intelligence/shared/` — `AnthropicLLM.structured()` via tool-use + forced `tool_choice` | Structured output already solved. No JSON-mode parsing, no regex. |
36	| Citation-grounding guard (`InvalidCitationError` at the evaluator boundary) | **This is your anti-hallucination story.** Extend it: verify the quoted span appears *verbatim* in the source text, not just that the doc id is real. |
37	| Three-state `Section.text` encoding (`None` / `""` / `"<text>"` → absent / empty / filled) | Your best original idea. Gives you a *sharper* verdict vocabulary than pass/fail. Keep it. |
38	| Deterministic-vs-LLM evaluation split | Maps directly to `rule_type: computed \| semantic`. Deterministic rules never hit the model — free speed, zero variance. |
39	| `asyncio.Semaphore(5)` fan-out pattern | Wall-time story. |
40	| `design/patient_spec.md` + the Marcus Rivera chart | **Biggest time save.** BPS intake + SOAP/DAP/DSAP notes already written and already have a designed gap. |
41	| Per-unit error isolation (one bad call → warning, not lost audit) | A single failed rule mid-demo degrades to amber instead of killing the run. |
42	
43	### Cut ruthlessly
44	
45	| Cut | Why |
46	|---|---|
47	| SimplePractice extraction / Playwright / auth cookie singleton | Invisible to judges, most fragile component, needs network + creds. Chart is a committed JSON file. |
48	| FHIR Bundle shaping | Ceremony. Judges don't see it. Plain documents with ids. |
49	| ASAM endpoint entirely | Unverifiable by a lay judge, and IP-blocked. |
50	| Applicability funnel (133 → 12 → 8) | Nice engineering, invisible payoff in 3 minutes. |
51	| pytest suite, VCR cassettes, mypy strict, Makefile | Four hours. |

79	## 3. Inputs
80	
81	### 3.1 Rulebook format
82	
83	12–15 rules in `rules/cms_psych.json`. Every rule carries the **verbatim** regulatory text plus an engineering-written evidence description (the paraphrase is fine here — it's your instruction to the model, not the citation shown to the judge).
84	
85	```json
86	{
87	  "rule_id": "482.61(c)(1)",
88	  "source": "42 CFR § 482.61",
89	  "source_url": "https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-482.61",
90	  "requirement_verbatim": "Each patient must have an individual comprehensive treatment plan that must be based on an inventory of the patient's strengths and disabilities.",
91	  "evidence_required": "Explicit description of patient assets, capabilities, skills, supports, or protective factors. Absence of documented deficits does NOT satisfy this.",
92	  "rule_type": "semantic",
93	  "scope_docs": ["treatment_plan", "bps_intake"]
94	}
95	```
96	
97	Computed rule example:
98	
99	```json
100	{
101	  "rule_id": "482.61(d)",
102	  "requirement_verbatim": "The frequency of progress notes is determined by the condition of the patient but must be recorded at least weekly for the first 2 months and at least once a month thereafter...",
103	  "rule_type": "computed",
104	  "handler": "progress_note_cadence"
105	}
106	```
107	
108	### 3.2 The four rules that carry the demo
109	
110	| Rule | Why it's in the deck |
111	|---|---|
112	| **§482.61(c)(1)** — treatment plan based on inventory of strengths and disabilities | **The headline finding.** Real charts document deficits exhaustively, strengths never. Judge ctrl-Fs "strength", finds nothing, learns something. This is your unfakeable moment. |
113	| **§482.61(a)(3)** — reasons for admission as stated by the patient and/or others significantly involved | **Proves semantic matching.** Text exists but it's the clinician's framing, not the patient's words. Resolves `unclear` (amber), not `fail`. |
114	| **§482.61(d)** — progress note cadence | **Computed, not semantic.** Pure date arithmetic. One row that is undeniably, checkably correct. |
115	| **§482.61(c)(1)(iv)** — responsibilities of each member of the treatment team | Chart has a signature block. The reg wants documented responsibilities. Different things. |
116	
117	### 3.3 Document corpus
118	
119	Start from `design/patient_spec.md`. Regenerate the chart as plain JSON:
120	
121	```json
122	{
123	  "doc_id": "bps_intake",
124	  "doc_type": "Biopsychosocial Assessment",
125	  "date": "2026-06-14",
126	  "author_role": "LCSW",
127	  "sections": [
128	    {"code": "hpi", "heading": "History of Present Illness", "text": "..."},
129	    {"code": "spiritual", "heading": "Spiritual/Religious", "text": ""}
130	  ]
131	}
132	```
133	
134	Keep the three-state encoding: `null` = section absent, `""` = present but blank, text = filled. Blank-but-present is a *better* finding than absent — "the template asked and the clinician skipped it" is a sharper sentence than "it's missing."
135	
136	**Contents:** BPS intake, treatment plan, three progress notes (SOAP / DAP / DSAP on different dates), discharge summary. Format inconsistency is deliberate — it's why a human can't skim.
137	
138	**Planted gaps (4):**
139	1. No strengths inventory anywhere → `fail` on (c)(1)
140	2. Admission reason in clinician voice only → `unclear` on (a)(3)
141	3. 23-day gap between progress notes 2 and 3 → `fail` on (d)
142	4. Signature block with no responsibilities → `fail` on (c)(1)(iv)
143	
144	Everything else passes cleanly. **Target the clean chart at ~10 green, 3 red, 1 amber.** All-red reads as broken; all-green reads as pointless.
145	
146	Generate the prose with Claude, not by hand. Give it the spec and the planted-gap list and tell it to write realistic clinical documentation that satisfies the other rules naturally.

150	## 4. Output
151	
152	### 4.1 Per-rule finding
153	
154	```json
155	{
156	  "rule_id": "482.61(c)(1)",
157	  "verdict": "fail",
158	  "evidence": null,
159	  "doc_id": null,
160	  "char_start": null,
161	  "char_end": null,
162	  "rationale": "No documentation of patient strengths, assets, or protective factors appears in the treatment plan or intake. The plan documents diagnoses and functional impairments only.",
163	  "confidence": "high",
164	  "mode": "semantic"
165	}
166	```
167	
168	A pass is identical but with `evidence` holding a **verbatim span** from the source and resolved offsets.
169	
170	### 4.2 The verification rule (non-negotiable)
171	
172	Server-side, before any finding reaches the client:
173	
174	```
175	if verdict == "pass":
176	    if evidence is None or evidence not in corpus[doc_id].full_text:
177	        verdict = "unclear"
178	        rationale += " [evidence span could not be verified]"
179	```
180	
181	This makes a hallucinated pass **structurally impossible**, and it gives you free highlighting via `str.find()`. It is also the single best sentence in your pitch: *the model cannot claim compliance without producing text that actually exists.*
182	
183	### 4.3 Verdict vocabulary
184	
185	- `pass` — green, verified span
186	- `fail` — red, no evidence found
187	- `unclear` — amber, evidence exists but doesn't clearly satisfy
188	
189	**Amber matters more than you think.** A wrong red row in front of judges costs you far more than a cautious amber one. Tune toward amber on ambiguity.
190

193	## 5. What the judge sees
194	
195	Three panes, `static/index.html`, vanilla JS, no build step.
196	
197	**Left — Chart.** Editable `<textarea>` per document, section headings visible. Scrollable. This is what the judge touches.
198	
199	**Middle — Findings.** One row per rule, streaming in via SSE as each resolves. Rule id, verbatim requirement text (truncated with expand), colored verdict chip.
200	
201	**Right — Citation detail.** Click a row → for a pass, the source text with the verified span highlighted; for a fail, the rule's full verbatim regulatory text and the rationale explaining what was searched and not found; a link to the eCFR section.
202	
203	**Design notes:**
204	- Rows must **stream**, not appear at once. Progressive fill reads as working; batch appearance reads as canned.
205	- Show a live counter: `14 rules · 10 pass · 3 fail · 1 unclear`.
206	- Show elapsed time on screen. It's your 40-minutes-to-90-seconds story, live.
207	- Re-run button must be one click and re-run only, not reload.

249	## 7. Demo script (3:00)
250	
251	**0:00–0:40 — The job.**
252	> "A compliance auditor reads every patient chart against a federal regulation and writes up what's missing. About 40 minutes a chart. Every psychiatric facility taking Medicare pays someone to do this, and they're all behind. This is 42 CFR 482.61 — you can pull it up right now, it's public."
253	
254	**0:40–1:20 — The run.**
255	Scroll the chart fast so the volume registers. Hit run. Rows stream. Click a green row: exact sentence highlighted. Click the strengths-inventory red row: verbatim regulation, and the rationale explaining nothing in the chart satisfies it.
256	> "Charts document what's wrong with a patient exhaustively. The regulation requires strengths. Almost nobody documents them."
257	
258	**1:20–2:30 — Hand it over. This is the demo.**
259	> "Delete anything you want from this chart."
260	
261	Judge deletes. Re-run. Row flips red, citing the hole they just made. Let them do it **three times**. Then have them *add* a line satisfying a currently-failing rule and watch it go green. An audience operating the thing beats an audience watching it, and it's the most direct possible answer to the fresh-input rule.
262	
263	**2:30–2:50 — The swap.**
264	Change the dropdown to SOC 2. Same engine, different domain, live.
265	> "Same engine. Different rulebook. That's a JSON file."
266	
267	**2:50–3:00 — Close.**
268	> "Forty minutes to ninety seconds. And the model can't claim compliance without quoting text that actually exists — we check every citation against the source before it hits your screen."
269	
270	---
271	
272	## 8. Failure modes and mitigations
273	
274	| Risk | Mitigation |
275	|---|---|
276	| A rule flaps between runs | Hour 4 stability pass. Any rule that flips gets its `evidence_required` tightened or gets cut. |
277	| Judge deletes something that breaks nothing | Rehearse the ask: *"delete the consent line, or the whole progress note from June 21."* Guide without scripting. |
278	| API latency spikes on conference wifi | Semaphore 5, and rows stream so partial results are visible. Have a recorded run open in a second tab — **narrate it as a recording if you use it**, never pass it off as live. |
279	| Judge asks "does this only work for healthcare" | The SOC 2 swap. Don't answer — show them. |
280	| Judge asks "what if the regulation changes" | Honest answer: the rulebook is data, not code; updating means editing JSON. |
281	| Judge asks "would a hospital trust this" | Honest answer: it's a first-pass triage that puts a human on the 4 findings instead of all 14 rules. Don't overclaim autonomy — the citation-verification design is what makes it reviewable. |
282

```text
1	"""Async Anthropic client wrapper with Pydantic structured outputs.
2	
3	Single LLM entry point for both ASAM (Endpoint 1) and TJC (Endpoint 2, future).
4	Endpoint-specific prompts live in their own modules
5	(``app/intelligence/asam/prompts.py``, future
6	``app/intelligence/compliance/prompts.py``); this module is purely the
7	transport plus structured-output machinery.
8	
9	Key behaviors:
10	    * **Temperature 0 by default** for reproducibility. Configurable via
11	      ``Settings.intelligence_llm_temperature``.
12	    * **Structured outputs via Anthropic tool-use**: define a tool whose
13	      ``input_schema`` is the response model's JSON schema, force tool_choice,
14	      and parse the tool input back to the Pydantic model. Tool-use is the
15	      documented and most reliable pattern for structured outputs on Claude.
16	    * **Retries with exponential backoff** on transient errors (rate limit,
17	      timeout, connection, 5xx). Configurable retry budget via
18	      ``Settings.intelligence_llm_max_retries``.
19	    * **PHI / IP safety**: prompt content is never logged at INFO. Bodies
20	      only appear in DEBUG logs when ``Settings.log_include_bodies`` is true.
21	      The Anthropic API key is held as ``SecretStr`` in settings and passed
22	      once to the SDK; it never appears in logs or exceptions.
23	
24	Reuse one ``AnthropicLLM`` instance across requests. Construct it in
25	``app/main.py:lifespan`` and stash on ``app.state.intelligence_llm`` so
26	the per-request work is just one method call.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import asyncio
32	import re
33	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
34	from typing import Any, Protocol, TypeVar
35	
36	import anthropic
37	import structlog
38	from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError
39	
40	from app.config import Settings
41	from app.intelligence.shared.errors import (
42	    LLMAuthError,
43	    LLMError,
44	    LLMRateLimitError,
45	    LLMTimeoutError,
46	    StructuredOutputParseError,
47	)
48	
49	logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
50	
51	_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4096
52	_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0
53	_RETRY_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER = 2.0
54	_PASCAL_TO_SNAKE_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])")
55	
56	T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)
57	
58	
59	class SupportsStructured(Protocol):
60	    """The minimal LLM-client interface the reasoning evaluators + orchestrators need.
61	
62	    ``AnthropicLLM`` (production) and the test doubles all satisfy this via duck
63	    typing. Both intelligence endpoints (ASAM, TJC compliance) consume this
64	    Protocol rather than depending on ``AnthropicLLM`` directly, so tests never
65	    construct a real Anthropic client. ``model_version`` is exposed so an
66	    orchestrator can stamp the model id on its output without the route layer
67	    threading it through.
68	    """
69	
70	    model_version: str
71	
72	    async def structured(
73	        self,
74	        *,
75	        system_prompt: str,
76	        user_prompt: str,
77	        response_model: type[T],
78	        max_tokens: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
79	    ) -> T: ...
80	
81	
82	class AnthropicLLM:
83	    """Async Anthropic client for structured-output generation.
84	
85	    The underlying SDK client is async and connection-pooled. Reuse one
86	    instance process-wide (via lifespan singleton) so per-request work is
87	    just the ``structured()`` call.
88	    """
89	
90	    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
91	        self._settings = settings
92	        self._client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(
93	            api_key=settings.anthropic_api_key.get_secret_value(),
94	        )
95	        self.model_version = settings.intelligence_llm_model
96	        self._temperature = settings.intelligence_llm_temperature
97	        self._max_retries = settings.intelligence_llm_max_retries
98	        self._log_include_bodies = settings.log_include_bodies
99	        logger.info(
100	            "intelligence.llm.client_ready",
101	            model=self.model_version,
102	            temperature=self._temperature,
103	            max_retries=self._max_retries,
104	        )
105	
106	    async def aclose(self) -> None:
107	        """Close the underlying HTTP client. Idempotent. Best-effort."""
108	        try:
109	            await self._client.close()
110	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — shutdown path, swallow
111	            pass
112	
113	    async def structured(
114	        self,
115	        *,
116	        system_prompt: str,
117	        user_prompt: str,
118	        response_model: type[T],
119	        max_tokens: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
120	    ) -> T:
121	        """Run a structured generation call and return a validated Pydantic instance.
122	
123	        The model is asked to invoke a single tool whose ``input_schema`` matches
124	        the response model's JSON schema. The tool's input is parsed back to
125	        the Pydantic model and returned.
126	
127	        Args:
128	            system_prompt: System message; describes the task and rubric.
129	            user_prompt: User message; contains the per-call data (e.g.,
130	                evidence pack).
131	            response_model: Pydantic class defining the expected output shape.
132	            max_tokens: Upper bound on response tokens.
133	
134	        Raises:
135	            LLMAuthError: API key invalid.
136	            LLMRateLimitError: rate limit exceeded after retry budget.
137	            LLMTimeoutError: connection/timeout errors after retry budget.
138	            StructuredOutputParseError: tool call missing or Pydantic
139	                validation failed.
140	            LLMError: other API errors.
141	        """
142	        tool = self._tool_for(response_model)
143	        log_ctx: dict[str, Any] = {
144	            "model": self.model_version,
145	            "tool_name": tool["name"],
146	            "response_model": response_model.__name__,
147	            "prompt_chars": len(system_prompt) + len(user_prompt),
148	        }
149	        if self._log_include_bodies:
150	            log_ctx["system_prompt"] = system_prompt
151	            log_ctx["user_prompt"] = user_prompt
152	        logger.debug("intelligence.llm.request", **log_ctx)
153	
154	        async def _call() -> anthropic.types.Message:
155	            return await self._client.messages.create(
156	                model=self.model_version,
157	                max_tokens=max_tokens,
158	                temperature=self._temperature,
159	                system=system_prompt,
160	                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}],
161	                tools=[tool],
162	                tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": tool["name"]},
163	            )
164	
165	        response = await self._with_retries(_call)
166	
167	        logger.info(
168	            "intelligence.llm.response",
169	            model=self.model_version,
170	            tool_name=tool["name"],
171	            response_model=response_model.__name__,
172	            input_tokens=response.usage.input_tokens,
173	            output_tokens=response.usage.output_tokens,
174	            stop_reason=response.stop_reason,
175	        )
176	
177	        return self._parse_tool_result(response, tool["name"], response_model)
178	
179	    # --- internals ----------------------------------------------------------
180	
181	    def _tool_for(self, response_model: type[BaseModel]) -> dict[str, Any]:
182	        """Build the Anthropic tool spec from a Pydantic model's JSON schema."""
183	        return {
184	            "name": f"emit_{_snake_case(response_model.__name__)}",
185	            "description": f"Emit a structured {response_model.__name__} response.",
186	            "input_schema": response_model.model_json_schema(),
187	        }
188	
189	    async def _with_retries(
190	        self,
191	        fn: Callable[[], Awaitable[anthropic.types.Message]],
192	    ) -> anthropic.types.Message:
193	        """Run an async callable with exponential-backoff retries on transient errors.
194	
195	        Retryable: ``RateLimitError``, ``APITimeoutError``, ``APIConnectionError``,
196	        ``APIStatusError`` with 5xx status. All others raise immediately.
197	        """
198	        attempt = 0
199	        delay = _RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SECONDS
200	        last_error: Exception | None = None
201	        while attempt <= self._max_retries:
202	            try:
203	                return await fn()
204	            except anthropic.AuthenticationError as e:
205	                raise LLMAuthError(f"Anthropic authentication failed: {e}") from e
206	            except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
207	                # Bug in our request shape; don't retry.
208	                raise LLMError(f"Bad request to Anthropic: {e}") from e
209	            except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
210	                last_error = e
211	                if attempt >= self._max_retries:
212	                    raise LLMRateLimitError(
213	                        f"Rate limit exhausted after {attempt} retries: {e}"
214	                    ) from e
215	                logger.warning(
216	                    "intelligence.llm.retry",
217	                    reason="rate_limit",
218	                    attempt=attempt + 1,
219	                    delay_s=delay,
220	                )
221	            except (anthropic.APITimeoutError, anthropic.APIConnectionError) as e:
222	                last_error = e
223	                if attempt >= self._max_retries:
224	                    raise LLMTimeoutError(
225	                        f"Transient error after {attempt} retries: {e}"
226	                    ) from e
227	                logger.warning(
228	                    "intelligence.llm.retry",
229	                    reason="transient",
230	                    attempt=attempt + 1,
231	                    delay_s=delay,
232	                    error=str(e),
233	                )
234	            except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
235	                if e.status_code >= 500:
236	                    last_error = e
237	                    if attempt >= self._max_retries:
238	                        raise LLMError(
239	                            f"Upstream {e.status_code} after {attempt} retries: {e}"
240	                        ) from e
241	                    logger.warning(
242	                        "intelligence.llm.retry",
243	                        reason="5xx",
244	                        status=e.status_code,
245	                        attempt=attempt + 1,
246	                        delay_s=delay,
247	                    )
248	                else:
249	                    raise LLMError(f"Anthropic API error {e.status_code}: {e}") from e
250	
251	            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
252	            attempt += 1
253	            delay *= _RETRY_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER
254	
255	        # Loop should exit via return/raise; guard for the typechecker.
256	        raise LLMError(f"Retry loop exhausted unexpectedly: {last_error}")
257	
258	    def _parse_tool_result(
259	        self,
260	        response: anthropic.types.Message,
261	        tool_name: str,
262	        response_model: type[T],
263	    ) -> T:
264	        """Find the tool_use block in the response and validate its input."""
265	        for block in response.content:
266	            if getattr(block, "type", None) != "tool_use":
267	                continue
268	            if getattr(block, "name", None) != tool_name:
269	                continue
270	            try:
271	                return response_model.model_validate(block.input)
272	            except ValidationError as e:
273	                raise StructuredOutputParseError(
274	                    f"LLM tool input failed Pydantic validation: {e}",
275	                    model=self.model_version,
276	                    raw_response=str(block.input)[:500],
277	                ) from e
278	        raise StructuredOutputParseError(
279	            f"LLM did not emit the expected tool '{tool_name}'. "
280	            f"Stop reason: {response.stop_reason}",
281	            model=self.model_version,
282	            raw_response=str(response.content)[:500],
283	        )
284	
285	
286	def _snake_case(name: str) -> str:
287	    """Convert PascalCase to snake_case for Anthropic tool naming."""
288	    return _PASCAL_TO_SNAKE_RE.sub("_", name).lower()
289
```

1	"""Citation type and construction helpers.
2	
3	A ``Citation`` points from a generated rationale (e.g., an
4	``ASAMAssessment.subdimension_ratings[i].rationale``) into the specific
5	location in the FHIR Bundle that the patient evidence came from. Citations
6	are how the intelligence layer grounds LLM-generated text in actual patient
7	data rather than hallucinated content.
8	
9	The Citation excerpt is verbatim text from the Bundle resource being cited —
10	never from external sources (ASAM IP, TJC IP, etc.) — capped at a reasonable
11	length so the citation acts as a pointer plus preview, not a duplicate of the
12	full source.
13	
14	Builders accept FHIR resources and produce a typed Citation with an
15	auto-extracted excerpt. Callers can override the excerpt explicitly when
16	they want to cite a specific phrase rather than the resource's default
17	representation.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
23	
24	from app.intelligence.shared.errors import CitationError
25	from app.schemas.common import CodeableConcept
26	from app.schemas.composition import Composition, Section
27	from app.schemas.condition import Condition
28	from app.schemas.observation import Observation
29	from app.schemas.questionnaire import QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireResponse
30	
31	_EXCERPT_MAX_LENGTH = 300
32	
33	
34	class Citation(BaseModel):
35	    """Pointer from a generated rationale to a specific Bundle location.
36	
37	    Fields:
38	        document_id: FHIR resource id this citation references
39	            (e.g., a Composition.id, QuestionnaireResponse.id, Condition.id).
40	        section_code: For Composition sections, the controlled coding in
41	            "<system>/<code>" form (e.g., "urn:perspectives:bps-section/15").
42	            Optional because not all citations target a section.
43	        item_link_id: For QuestionnaireResponse items, the linkId of the
44	            cited item. Optional.
45	        excerpt: Short verbatim text from the cited Bundle resource. Used by
46	            reviewers to verify the citation without traversing the Bundle.
47	            Required and non-empty.
48	    """
49	
50	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
51	
52	    document_id: str
53	    section_code: str | None = None
54	    item_link_id: str | None = None
55	    excerpt: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
56	
57	
58	# --- Builders ----------------------------------------------------------------
59	
60	
61	def cite_section(
62	    composition: Composition,
63	    section: Section,
64	    *,
65	    excerpt: str | None = None,
66	) -> Citation:
67	    """Construct a Citation for a ``Composition.section``.
68	
69	    If ``excerpt`` is omitted, extracts a truncated preview from ``section.text``.
70	    Empty sections (state="empty" or text=None) yield a labeled placeholder
71	    excerpt so the citation still conveys what was cited.
72	    """
73	    section_code_str = _section_code_str(section.code)
74	    extracted = excerpt if excerpt is not None else _section_excerpt(section)
75	    if not extracted:
76	        raise CitationError(
77	            f"Cannot construct Citation for section {section.title!r}: no usable excerpt."
78	        )
79	    return Citation(
80	        document_id=composition.id,
81	        section_code=section_code_str,
82	        excerpt=extracted,
83	    )
84	
85	
86	def cite_questionnaire_item(
87	    qr: QuestionnaireResponse,
88	    item: QuestionnaireItem,
89	    *,
90	    excerpt: str | None = None,
91	) -> Citation:
92	    """Construct a Citation for one item in a ``QuestionnaireResponse``.
93	
94	    Default excerpt format: ``"Q: <question> | A: <answer label>"``.
95	    """
96	    extracted = excerpt if excerpt is not None else _item_excerpt(item)
97	    if not extracted:
98	        raise CitationError(
99	            f"Cannot construct Citation for QR item {item.linkId!r}: no usable excerpt."
100	        )
101	    return Citation(
102	        document_id=qr.id,
103	        item_link_id=item.linkId,
104	        excerpt=extracted,
105	    )
106	
107	
108	def cite_observation(
109	    obs: Observation,
110	    *,
111	    excerpt: str | None = None,
112	) -> Citation:
113	    """Construct a Citation for an ``Observation`` (e.g., DAST-10 score).
114	
115	    Default excerpt format: ``"<code display>: <value> <unit> — <interpretation>"``.
116	    """
117	    extracted = excerpt if excerpt is not None else _observation_excerpt(obs)
118	    if not extracted:
119	        raise CitationError(
120	            f"Cannot construct Citation for Observation {obs.id}: no usable excerpt."
121	        )
122	    return Citation(
123	        document_id=obs.id,
124	        excerpt=extracted,
125	    )
126	
127	
128	def cite_condition(
129	    cond: Condition,
130	    *,
131	    excerpt: str | None = None,
132	) -> Citation:
133	    """Construct a Citation for a ``Condition``.
134	
135	    Default excerpt format: ``"<code display> (<verification status>)"``.
136	    """
137	    extracted = excerpt if excerpt is not None else _condition_excerpt(cond)
138	    if not extracted:
139	        raise CitationError(
140	            f"Cannot construct Citation for Condition {cond.id}: no usable excerpt."
141	        )
142	    return Citation(
143	        document_id=cond.id,
144	        excerpt=extracted,
145	    )
146	
147	
148	# --- Internal excerpt extractors --------------------------------------------
149	
150	
151	def _truncate(text: str, limit: int = _EXCERPT_MAX_LENGTH) -> str:
152	    text = text.strip()
153	    if len(text) <= limit:
154	        return text
155	    return text[: limit - 1].rstrip() + "…"  # ellipsis
156	
157	
158	def _section_code_str(code: CodeableConcept | None) -> str | None:
159	    if code is None or not code.coding:
160	        return None
161	    first = code.coding[0]
162	    return f"{first.system}/{first.code}"
163	
164	
165	def _section_excerpt(section: Section) -> str:
166	    if section.text:
167	        return _truncate(section.text)
168	    return f"<empty section: {section.title}>"
169	
170	
171	def _item_excerpt(item: QuestionnaireItem) -> str:
172	    answer_label = _item_answer_label(item)
173	    if answer_label is None:
174	        return _truncate(f"Q: {item.text} | A: <no answer>")
175	    return _truncate(f"Q: {item.text} | A: {answer_label}")
176	
177	
178	def _item_answer_label(item: QuestionnaireItem) -> str | None:
179	    if not item.answer:
180	        return None
181	    first = item.answer[0]
182	    if first.valueCoding is not None and first.valueCoding.display:
183	        return first.valueCoding.display
184	    if first.valueString is not None:
185	        return first.valueString
186	    if first.valueBoolean is not None:
187	        return str(first.valueBoolean)
188	    if first.valueInteger is not None:
189	        return str(first.valueInteger)
190	    if first.valueDecimal is not None:
191	        return str(first.valueDecimal)
192	    return None
193	
194	
195	def _observation_excerpt(obs: Observation) -> str:
196	    code_display = (
197	        obs.code.text
198	        or (obs.code.coding[0].display if obs.code.coding else None)
199	        or "observation"
200	    )
201	    value_str: str = "<no value>"
202	    if obs.valueQuantity is not None:
203	        unit = obs.valueQuantity.unit or ""
204	        value_str = f"{obs.valueQuantity.value} {unit}".strip()
205	    elif obs.valueCodeableConcept is not None:
206	        if obs.valueCodeableConcept.text:
207	            value_str = obs.valueCodeableConcept.text
208	        elif obs.valueCodeableConcept.coding:
209	            value_str = obs.valueCodeableConcept.coding[0].display or obs.valueCodeableConcept.coding[0].code
210	    interp_str = ""
211	    if obs.interpretation:
212	        first_interp = obs.interpretation[0]
213	        label = first_interp.text or (first_interp.coding[0].display if first_interp.coding else None)
214	        if label:
215	            interp_str = f" — {label}"  # em-dash
216	    return _truncate(f"{code_display}: {value_str}{interp_str}")
217	
218	
219	def _condition_excerpt(cond: Condition) -> str:
220	    code_display = (
221	        cond.code.text
222	        or (cond.code.coding[0].display if cond.code.coding else None)
223	        or (cond.code.coding[0].code if cond.code.coding else "condition")
224	    )
225	    verification = ""
226	    if cond.verificationStatus is not None and cond.verificationStatus.coding:
227	        verification = f" ({cond.verificationStatus.coding[0].code})"
228	    return _truncate(f"{code_display}{verification}")

1	"""LLM-mediated per-EP verdict for the TJC compliance audit.
2	
3	Given an ``ElementOfPerformance`` (``evaluation_mode == "llm"``) and its
4	``CompliancePack``, this module:
5	
6	1. Builds the system + user prompts via ``prompts.py``.
7	2. Calls the LLM with structured output targeting ``ElementFindingDraft``.
8	3. Validates each citation's ``document_id`` against the evidence pack
9	   (anti-hallucination guard).
10	4. Merges the draft with catalog metadata (``ep_id``, ``standard_id``,
11	   ``requirement_text``, ``evaluation_mode``) into a final ``ElementFinding``.
12	
13	There is one LLM call per EP — exactly ASAM's one-unit-per-call shape, reused
14	nearly verbatim. There is no rating-scale validation step: ``verdict`` is a
15	``Literal``, so Pydantic rejects an off-vocabulary value at draft-parse time.
16	
17	``SupportsStructured`` is imported from the shared LLM module —
18	``compliance/ -> shared/`` is allowed; ``compliance/ -> asam/`` is not.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import structlog
24	
25	from app.intelligence.compliance.errors import ComplianceAuditError, InvalidCitationError
26	from app.intelligence.compliance.prompts import build_system_prompt, build_user_prompt
27	from app.intelligence.compliance.schemas import (
28	    Citation,
29	    CompliancePack,
30	    ElementFinding,
31	    ElementFindingDraft,
32	    ElementOfPerformance,
33	)
34	from app.intelligence.shared.llm import SupportsStructured
35	
36	logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
37	
38	
39	async def evaluate_element(
40	    ep: ElementOfPerformance,
41	    pack: CompliancePack,
42	    llm: SupportsStructured,
43	    *,
44	    max_tokens: int = 4096,
45	) -> ElementFinding:
46	    """Evaluate one llm-mode element of performance against its evidence pack.
47	
48	    Raises:
49	        ComplianceAuditError: the pack's ``ep_id`` does not match ``ep`` (a
50	            dispatcher bug).
51	        InvalidCitationError: a citation's ``document_id`` is not in the pack.
52	        StructuredOutputParseError / LLMError + subclasses: from the LLM
53	            transport.
54	    """
55	    if pack.ep_id != ep.ep_id:
56	        raise ComplianceAuditError(
57	            f"Evidence pack ep_id={pack.ep_id!r} does not match element "
58	            f"id={ep.ep_id!r}. Did the dispatcher mis-route?"
59	        )
60	
61	    logger.info(
62	        "intelligence.compliance.evaluator.start",
63	        ep_id=ep.ep_id,
64	        evidence_count=len(pack.items),
65	        sufficient=pack.sufficient,
66	    )
67	
68	    draft = await _call_llm(ep, pack, llm, max_tokens=max_tokens)
69	    _validate_citations(draft.citations, pack, ep)
70	    finding = _merge_into_finding(draft, ep)
71	
72	    logger.info(
73	        "intelligence.compliance.evaluator.done",
74	        ep_id=ep.ep_id,
75	        verdict=finding.verdict,
76	        confidence=finding.confidence,
77	        citation_count=len(finding.citations),
78	    )
79	    return finding
80	
81	
82	# --- internals ---------------------------------------------------------------
83	
84	
85	async def _call_llm(
86	    ep: ElementOfPerformance,
87	    pack: CompliancePack,
88	    llm: SupportsStructured,
89	    *,
90	    max_tokens: int,
91	) -> ElementFindingDraft:
92	    """Build prompts and call the LLM for a single EP verdict."""
93	    return await llm.structured(
94	        system_prompt=build_system_prompt(),
95	        user_prompt=build_user_prompt(ep, pack),
96	        response_model=ElementFindingDraft,
97	        max_tokens=max_tokens,
98	    )
99	
100	
101	def _validate_citations(
102	    citations: list[Citation],
103	    pack: CompliancePack,
104	    ep: ElementOfPerformance,
105	) -> None:
106	    """Each citation's ``document_id`` must match an evidence item in the pack.
107	
108	    The anti-hallucination guard: the pack is the only Bundle window the LLM
109	    saw, so a fabricated ``document_id`` is almost always invented.
110	    """
111	    valid_doc_ids = {item.document_id for item in pack.items}
112	    for idx, citation in enumerate(citations):
113	        if citation.document_id not in valid_doc_ids:
114	            raise InvalidCitationError(
115	                f"Citation #{idx} for EP {ep.ep_id} references "
116	                f"document_id={citation.document_id!r}, which does not appear "
117	                f"in the evidence pack. Valid document_ids: "
118	                f"{sorted(valid_doc_ids)}. Excerpt: {citation.excerpt[:80]!r}"
119	            )
120	
121	
122	def _merge_into_finding(
123	    draft: ElementFindingDraft,
124	    ep: ElementOfPerformance,
125	) -> ElementFinding:
126	    """Merge the LLM-emitted draft with catalog metadata into a full finding."""
127	    return ElementFinding(
128	        ep_id=ep.ep_id,
129	        standard_id=ep.standard_id,
130	        requirement_text=ep.requirement_text,
131	        evaluation_mode=ep.evaluation_mode,
132	        verdict=draft.verdict,
133	        rationale=draft.rationale,
134	        citations=draft.citations,
135	        confidence=draft.confidence,
136	        remediation_hint=draft.remediation_hint,
137	    )
138

1	"""Per-EP prompt builders for the LLM-mediated compliance evaluator.
2	
3	Prompts are GENERATED from the ``ElementOfPerformance`` catalog entry + the
4	``CompliancePack`` at call time — no per-EP hardcoded prompt strings. The
5	template reads the EP's ``requirement_text`` (an original-wording paraphrase —
6	IP discipline, see ``docs/ip_compliance.md``) and the evidence items.
7	
8	Public API:
9	    build_system_prompt() -> str
10	        Shared across all EP evaluators. Defines the auditor role, the verdict
11	        vocabulary, citation-grounding rules, and the remediation-hint contract.
12	
13	    build_user_prompt(ep, pack) -> str
14	        Per-call. Emits an EP header (including the ``**EP ID:**`` marker the
15	        test double dispatches on), the requirement, the verdict scale, the
16	        evidence pack, a citation guide, and the call to action.
17	
18	The evaluator calls ``llm.structured()`` with these prompts and a
19	``response_model`` of ``ElementFindingDraft``; the draft is merged with catalog
20	metadata to construct the final ``ElementFinding``.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	from app.intelligence.compliance.schemas import CompliancePack, ElementOfPerformance
26	
27	# =============================================================================
28	# System prompt — shared across all EPs
29	# =============================================================================
30	
31	_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
32	You are a behavioral-health compliance auditor. You judge whether ONE element \
33	of performance (EP) from a Joint Commission Care, Treatment, and Services (CTS) \
34	standard is met by a single patient's chart.
35	
36	Your job is:
37	
38	1. Read the EP requirement. It states, in plain terms, what the chart must \
39	document for this element to be met.
40	
41	2. Read the evidence drawn from the patient's chart. Each evidence item has a \
42	stable reference ID (like `[ev_001]`) that you must use when citing it.
43	
44	3. Pick exactly one verdict:
45	   - "met" — the evidence shows the requirement is satisfied.
46	   - "not_met" — the evidence shows the requirement is NOT satisfied (a \
47	documentation gap, a missing element, or a dismissive non-answer).
48	   - "partial" — the requirement is addressed but incompletely (e.g., a plan \
49	goal exists but is vague rather than measurable).
50	   - "not_chart_auditable" — the evidence pack is empty or contains nothing \
51	relevant to this requirement, so the chart cannot answer it. Use this ONLY \
52	when you genuinely cannot judge from the evidence given.
53	
54	4. Write a rationale of 2 to 4 sentences. Ground every claim in specific \
55	evidence items by their bracketed IDs (e.g., "Per ev_002 the plan states..."). \
56	Reference the SPECIFIC text in the chart that supports your verdict. Do not \
57	invent details that are not in the evidence pack.
58	
59	5. Construct Citation objects pointing back to the evidence items you \
60	referenced. Each Citation must:
61	   - Use the `document_id` exactly as it appears on the cited evidence item.
62	   - Use the `section_code` from the evidence item if present, else omit.
63	   - Use the `item_link_id` from the evidence item if present, else omit.
64	   - Set `excerpt` to a short verbatim phrase (under 200 characters) from the \
65	evidence item's content — the actual chart text you are citing.
66	
67	6. Assign a confidence level: "high" (the evidence directly settles it), \
68	"medium" (reasonable inference required), or "low" (sparse or conflicting \
69	evidence).
70	
71	7. If the verdict is "not_met" or "partial", set `remediation_hint` to ONE \
72	concrete, specific action the provider should take to come into compliance \
73	(e.g., "Document a measurable target and a review date for each treatment \
74	goal."). Keep it grounded in the EP requirement. For "met" verdicts leave \
75	`remediation_hint` null.
76	
77	Emit your response as a single structured tool call. Do not include narrative \
78	text outside the structured response. Judge only this one EP — not the \
79	standard overall, and not other standards.\
80	"""
81	
82	
83	def build_system_prompt() -> str:
84	    """Return the shared system prompt for the per-EP compliance evaluator."""
85	    return _SYSTEM_PROMPT
86	
87	
88	# =============================================================================
89	# User prompt — per-EP + per-call
90	# =============================================================================
91	
92	
93	def build_user_prompt(ep: ElementOfPerformance, pack: CompliancePack) -> str:
94	    """Build the per-call user prompt for one element of performance."""
95	    parts = [
96	        _format_ep_header(ep),
97	        _format_requirement(ep),
98	        _format_verdict_scale(),
99	        _format_evidence_pack(pack),
100	        _format_citation_guide(pack),
101	        _format_call_to_action(),
102	    ]
103	    return "\n\n".join(parts)
104	
105	
106	def _format_ep_header(ep: ElementOfPerformance) -> str:
107	    # The `**EP ID:**` line is load-bearing: the test double parses the EP id
108	    # out of it to dispatch canned responses. Keep the format stable.
109	    return (
110	        "# Element of performance to audit\n"
111	        "\n"
112	        f"- **Standard:** `{ep.standard_id}`\n"
113	        f"- **EP ID:** `{ep.ep_id}`"
114	    )
115	
116	
117	def _format_requirement(ep: ElementOfPerformance) -> str:
118	    return (
119	        "# What this element of performance requires\n"
120	        "\n"
121	        f"{ep.requirement_text}"
122	    )
123	
124	
125	def _format_verdict_scale() -> str:
126	    return (
127	        "# Valid verdicts\n"
128	        "\n"
129	        "Pick exactly one:\n"
130	        "\n"
131	        "- `met` — the chart documents what the requirement asks for.\n"
132	        "- `not_met` — the chart does not (a gap, a missing element, or a "
133	        "dismissive non-answer like a bare 'N/A').\n"
134	        "- `partial` — addressed but incompletely.\n"
135	        "- `not_chart_auditable` — the evidence pack has nothing relevant; the "
136	        "chart cannot answer this. Use sparingly."
137	    )
138	
139	
140	def _format_evidence_pack(pack: CompliancePack) -> str:
141	    """Format the evidence pack as a referenceable list."""
142	    if not pack.items and not pack.pack_notes and pack.sufficient:
143	        return (
144	            "# Evidence from patient chart\n"
145	            "\n"
146	            "No evidence items were found in the patient's chart for this "
147	            "element of performance. Set the verdict to `not_chart_auditable` "
148	            "and explain in your rationale."
149	        )
150	
151	    lines = ["# Evidence from patient chart", ""]
152	    if pack.items:
153	        lines.append(
154	            "Each item below is one piece of evidence pulled from the patient's "
155	            "chart. Reference items in your rationale by their bracketed ID tag "
156	            "(e.g., `[ev_003]`). Build Citation objects from these items."
157	        )
158	        lines.append("")
159	        for item in pack.items:
160	            lines.append(f"## `[{item.reference_id}]` {item.label}")
161	            lines.append("")
162	            metadata_bits = [f"`document_id`: `{item.document_id}`"]
163	            if item.section_code:
164	                metadata_bits.append(f"`section_code`: `{item.section_code}`")
165	            if item.item_link_id:
166	                metadata_bits.append(f"`item_link_id`: `{item.item_link_id}`")
167	            metadata_bits.append(f"source_type: `{item.source_type}`")
168	            lines.append("- " + "  · ".join(metadata_bits))
169	            lines.append("")
170	            lines.append(item.content)
171	            lines.append("")
172	
173	    if pack.pack_notes:
174	        lines.append("## Pack notes")
175	        lines.append("")
176	        lines.append(
177	            "Absences or contextual flags the evidence-gathering step recorded. "
178	            "Weigh them; cite them only if they materially change the verdict."
179	        )
180	        lines.append("")
181	        for note in pack.pack_notes:
182	            lines.append(f"- {note}")
183	        lines.append("")
184	
185	    if not pack.sufficient:
186	        lines.append("## Sufficiency flag")
187	        lines.append("")
188	        lines.append(
189	            f"The evidence pack was pre-flagged as insufficient. Reason: "
190	            f"{pack.insufficient_reason} Set the verdict to "
191	            f"`not_chart_auditable` and restate the reason in your rationale."
192	        )
193	
194	    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip()

Both Dim 4 subdimensions rate at `B` — likelihood of continued risky substance use is moderate, and the destabilizing-consequence horizon (job loss within 30-day PIP, marital dissolution within wife's ultimatum window) qualifies as imminent. His Dim 5 functional capacity and recovery environment are adequate for outpatient (no residential indication).

106	
107	Per the 4th-edition methodology, Dim 6 is a *post-recommendation* dialogue between clinician and patient about willingness and ability to engage at the recommended level. Will likely attend IOP given external pressure but may disengage if pressure relaxes.
112	- **Ability:** *Adequate.* Schedule permits evening IOP (3 evenings/week). Insurance covers IOP via Blue Cross Blue Shield IL PPO. Transportation available. Wife supports attendance. No caregiving conflicts (children are school-aged; partner present).
113	- **Adjustment needed:** *No.* Marcus is able to attend the recommended Level 2.1 and is willing enough that motivational interviewing in early sessions is the appropriate response to ambivalence — not a downward LoC adjustment.

115	- **Discrepancy reasons:** None.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls.

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

## Language Detection

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in:

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:

   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` → **Python** — read from `python/`
   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` → **TypeScript** — read from `typescript/`
   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) → **TypeScript** — JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` → **Java** — read from `java/`
   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` → **Java** — Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` → **Java** — Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.go`, `go.mod` → **Go** — read from `go/`
   - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` → **Ruby** — read from `ruby/`
   - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` → **C#** — read from `csharp/`
   - `*.php`, `composer.json` → **PHP** — read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

   - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
   - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

---

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

---

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

### Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`) — most capable widely released model

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work; everything below also applies to **Claude Mythos 5** (`claude-mythos-5`, Project Glasswing — same capabilities, pricing, and API surface; successor to the invitation-only `claude-mythos-preview`). 1M context window (the maximum is also the default), 128K max output. Key API differences from Opus-tier — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 for details:

- **Thinking is always on** — omit the `thinking` parameter entirely (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`). Any other explicit configuration is rejected: `{type: "disabled"}` and `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` both return a 400. Control depth with `output_config.effort` (supports `low` through `xhigh` and `max`).
- **The raw chain of thought is never returned** — responses carry regular `thinking` blocks (not `redacted_thinking`): `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary, `"omitted"` (the default) leaves the `thinking` field as an empty string. Replay rules: pass thinking blocks back unchanged on the same model; other models drop them silently (unbilled — nothing to strip); details in `shared/model-migration.md`.
- **Tokenizer** — same tokenizer as Opus 4.8 (introduced with Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from Opus 4.7/4.8; per-token pricing differs. Coming from Opus 4.6, Sonnet, Haiku, or older, re-baseline with `count_tokens` (the Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses ~1×–1.35× as many tokens).
- **`refusal` stop reason — handle it, and opt into fallbacks by default** — safety classifiers may decline a request (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: "refusal"`, with a `stop_details` category); always check `stop_reason` before reading `content`. **When you write `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` code, include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter by default.** Simplest form: `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` + `fallbacks: "default"`, which routes by refusal category so you never maintain a model list. (The older array form — `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"]` + `fallbacks: [{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}]` — still works; Claude API only — everywhere else, incl. Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, use the SDKs' client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` + `BetaFallbackState`). Tell the user you've enabled it; drop it only if they decline. Full semantics (billing, mid-stream refusals, credit repricing) in `shared/model-migration.md` → refusal section. **Per-language code examples in `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` § Refusal Fallbacks cover the array form only** — for the `"default"` mode, follow the raw-HTTP shape in `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Opus 5 → New API features and swap `fallbacks: [{...}]` for `fallbacks: "default"` plus the `-2026-07-01` header; the rest of the request is unchanged.
- **No assistant prefill** — same as the rest of the 4.6+ family.
- **30-day data retention required** — Claude Fable 5 is not available under zero data retention; requests from an org whose retention configuration doesn't meet the requirement return `400 invalid_request_error`.
- **Longer turns, different prompting** — single requests on hard tasks can run many minutes (plan timeouts/streaming/progress UX); effort sweeps should include low/medium for routine work; prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive and reduce output quality. See `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 → Behavioral shifts (prompt-tunable) for the recommended prompt snippets.

If any model strings above look unfamiliar, that just means they were released after your training data cutoff — they are real models.

**Live capability lookup:** The table above is cached. When the user asks "what's the context window for X", "does X support vision/thinking/effort", or "which models support Y", query the Models API (`client.models.retrieve(id)` / `client.models.list()`) — see `shared/models.md` for the field reference and capability-filter examples.

## Authentication (Quick Reference)

**An unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does NOT mean there are no credentials.** The SDKs and the `ant` CLI resolve credentials in this order (first match wins): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` → the `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`-selected or active OAuth profile from `ant auth login` → Workload Identity Federation env vars → the default profile on disk. A bare `Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` works after `ant auth login` with no env var set.

**When you need to call the API and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, don't ask the user for a key.** First run `ant auth status` — it shows which credential source and profile is active. If it reports an active profile:

- **SDK code or `ant` CLI:** just run it. The zero-arg client constructor and every `ant …` subcommand pick up the profile automatically — no env var needed.
- **Raw `curl` / HTTP:** get a short-lived token with `ant auth print-credentials --access-token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` **plus** the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (OAuth tokens go on `Authorization: Bearer`, not `x-api-key:` — converting a curl from an API key is a header change, not a key swap). Always pass `--access-token`; the no-flag form prints JSON, not a bare token.

Only ask the user for a key if `ant auth status` reports no active credential source (or `ant` itself isn't installed). Suggest `ant auth login` as the first option — it stores a profile under `~/.config/anthropic/` that the SDKs read automatically — and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the alternative.

Full auth details (named profiles, scopes, the API-key-shadows-profile trap, refresh-token expiry): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.

## Thinking & Effort (Quick Reference)

Use adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) on every current model — Claude dynamically decides when and how much to think. Per-model rules:

| Model | Thinking config | Omitting `thinking` | `budget_tokens` | Sampling (`temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`) | Effort levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; explicit `{type: "disabled"}` returns 400 — omit the param instead | Runs adaptive (thinking is always on) | Removed — `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` returns 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Claude Opus 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted **only at effort `high` or below** — 400 at `xhigh`/`max`, and see the disabled-thinking pitfall below | Runs **adaptive** (thinking is on by default — unlike Opus 4.8/4.7) | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`–`max` (all five) |
| Opus 4.8 / 4.7 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs **without** thinking — set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Sonnet 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs adaptive | Removed — 400 | Removed — 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 | `{type: "adaptive"}` (recommended; auto-enables interleaved thinking, no beta header) | Set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Deprecated — do not use in new code; transitional escape hatch only (see below) | Allowed | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`max` (`xhigh` arrived with Opus 4.7) |
| Older (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, …) — only if explicitly requested | `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | No thinking | Required for thinking; must be less than `max_tokens`, minimum 1024 — errors otherwise | Allowed | `effort` works on Opus 4.5 (`low`/`medium`/`high` only — no `xhigh`/`max`); errors on Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 |

Opus 4.8 keeps the same request surface as 4.7 (no new breaking changes) — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Opus 4.8 for the behavioral re-tuning, and → Migrating to Opus 4.7 for the full breaking-change list when coming from 4.6 or earlier. With `thinking` disabled, Opus 4.8 may write longer reasoning into the visible response — leave adaptive thinking on, or add a final-answer-only instruction (see the migration guide).

- **Effort (GA, no beta header):** `output_config: {effort: "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max"}` — inside `output_config`, not top-level; default `high` (equivalent to omitting it). Controls thinking depth and overall token spend; combine with adaptive thinking for the best cost-quality tradeoffs. `xhigh` (added on Opus 4.7, between `high` and `max`) is the best setting for most coding and agentic use cases on Fable 5 / Opus 4.7/4.8 / Sonnet 5, and the default in Claude Code; effort matters more on those models than on any prior model in their tier — re-tune it when migrating, and run long-horizon/agentic tasks at `high`/`xhigh` with the full task spec given up front. Use a minimum of `high` for intelligence-sensitive work, `max` when correctness matters more than cost, and `low` for subagents or simple tasks — lower effort means fewer and more-consolidated tool calls, less preamble, and terser confirmations (`high` is often the sweet spot balancing quality and token efficiency).
- **Thinking display — `"omitted"` by default on Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / Sonnet 5:** `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary of the reasoning; `"omitted"` (the default on all six — a silent change from Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, where it was `"summarized"`) streams `thinking` blocks with empty text. `display` controls visibility only — thinking happens and is billed the same under every setting; the raw chain of thought is never exposed on any model. If you stream reasoning to users, the default looks like a long pause before output — set `thinking: {type: "adaptive", display: "summarized"}` explicitly. (Independent of display, echo thinking blocks back unchanged when continuing on the same model; other models silently ignore them — see the migration guide.)
- **When the user asks for "extended thinking", a "thinking budget", or `budget_tokens`:** always use Fable 5, Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, or 4.6 with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` — the fixed thinking-token-budget concept is deprecated and adaptive thinking replaces it. Do NOT use `budget_tokens` for new 4.6/4.7/4.8 code and do NOT switch to an older model just because the user mentions it. *Gradual-migration carve-out:* `budget_tokens` is still functional on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 only, as a transitional escape hatch for existing code that needs a hard token ceiling before you've tuned `effort` — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Transitional escape hatch. It is fully removed on Fable 5, Opus 5/4.7/4.8, and Sonnet 5.

## Compaction (Quick Reference)

**Beta, Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6.** For long-running conversations that may exceed the 1M context window, enable server-side compaction. The API automatically summarizes earlier context when it approaches the trigger threshold (default: 150K tokens). Requires beta header `compact-2026-01-12`.

**Critical:** Append `response.content` (not just the text) back to your messages on every turn. Compaction blocks in the response must be preserved — the API uses them to replace the compacted history on the next request. Extracting only the text string and appending that will silently lose the compaction state.

See `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Compaction section) for code examples. Full docs via WebFetch in `shared/live-sources.md`.

---

## Prompt Caching (Quick Reference)

**Prefix match.** Any byte change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. Render order is `tools` → `system` → `messages`. Keep stable content first (frozen system prompt, deterministic tool list), put volatile content (timestamps, per-request IDs, varying questions) after the last `cache_control` breakpoint.

**Mid-conversation operator instructions** (Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5; not Claude Sonnet 5; no beta header): append `{"role": "system", ...}` to `messages[]` instead of editing top-level `system`. Preserves the cached history prefix and is the prompt-injection-safe operator channel. See `shared/prompt-caching.md` § Mid-conversation system messages.

**Top-level auto-caching** (`cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on `messages.create()`) is the simplest option when you don't need fine-grained placement. Max 4 breakpoints per request. Minimum cacheable prefix is ~1024 tokens — shorter prefixes silently won't cache.

**Verify with `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`** — if it's zero across repeated requests, a silent invalidator is at work (`datetime.now()` in system prompt, unsorted JSON, varying tool set).

For placement patterns, architectural guidance, and the silent-invalidator audit checklist: read `shared/prompt-caching.md`. Language-specific syntax: `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Prompt Caching section).

## Fast Mode (Quick Reference)

**Research preview, Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only** — Claude API and Managed Agents, not Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry. Opus 4.7 fast mode has been removed: `speed: "fast"` on 4.7 returns an error. Fast mode on Claude Opus 5 is priced at $10 / $50 per MTok. Fast mode runs the same model at up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second, at premium pricing. Three things are required on every request: use the **beta** messages endpoint (`client.beta.messages.…`), pass the beta flag `fast-mode-2026-02-01`, and set `speed: "fast"` as a top-level request parameter (not a header, not in `extra_body`).

```python
client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5", max_tokens=4096,
    speed="fast", betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"],
    messages=[...],
)
```

| Language | Beta flag | Speed parameter |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed="fast"` |
| TypeScript / Ruby | `betas: ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed: "fast"` |
| Go | `[]anthropic.AnthropicBeta{anthropic.AnthropicBetaFastMode2026_02_01}` | `Speed: anthropic.BetaMessageNewParamsSpeedFast` |
| Java | `.addBeta(AnthropicBeta.FAST_MODE_2026_02_01)` | `.speed(MessageCreateParams.Speed.FAST)` |
| C# | `Betas = ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `Speed = Speed.Fast` (`Anthropic.Models.Beta.Messages`) |
| PHP | `betas: ['fast-mode-2026-02-01']` | `speed: 'fast'` |
| cURL | `anthropic-beta: fast-mode-2026-02-01` header | `"speed": "fast"` in body |

`response.usage.speed` reports which speed was used. Fast mode has its own rate limit separate from standard Opus; on 429, either retry after the `retry-after` delay or drop `speed` and fall back to standard (note: switching speed invalidates prompt cache). Not available with Batch API, Priority Tier, Claude Platform on AWS, or third-party platforms.

**Priority Tier does not cover Claude Opus 5.** It is supported on every other current model, including Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, but Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Mythos 5, and Mythos Preview are excluded — a Priority Tier request naming one of them fails validation.
